name: s4-hedged-nbp
title: 0%-hedged vGOLD pair on 49990013, sized from equity: equity below zero (server valuation) with no used margin, never stopped out, closed by each other

steps.text: SB Hedge NBP on vGOLD: leverage 1000, stop-out 20, markup 60 pips (6.00: a BUY fills 6.00 above the ask and an open SELL is valued at the ask + 6.00), commission 50 per lot, hedged margin 0. So EACH leg costs about 680 per lot the moment it opens (630 valuation + 50 commission) and the pair about 1360. SELL sized so its FULL margin is 18% of equity: 600 -> 0.53 lot, after it equity ~240 on margin ~106 = level ~225% (clear of the 20% stop-out AND of the 100% margin call, so the lone first leg is never closed). BUY = the same lots: the pair's used margin is 0 (level null) and equity ~ 600 - 0.53 x 1360 = -121. A hedging order that does not raise used margin is always accepted (lib/margin.ts), so the second leg is not refused at negative equity. The ramps move both legs equally: equity stays negative, level stays null, nothing is stopped out. The pair is closed BY EACH OTHER in one request (closing one leg first would leave the other alone on negative equity and the stop-out would take it). No write-off is expected: close-by settles BOTH legs at one raw price, so the SELL's valuation markup is never realized and only the BUY's is (0.53 x 6.30 x 100 = 334): the balance ends ~213 (2026-09-29 run: 213.10). The equity was negative only in the server's valuation of the open pair (~-121; the bot's own estimate values the SELL at the raw ask and shows ~+197). What S4 proves: negative equity at a null margin level (used margin 0) is NEVER stopped out, through ramps both ways. The write-off belongs to a scenario that breaks the hedge.
